solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Men on e.g. kitchen duty, bore before special do (12, two words)

parts.note: to bore someone is to tire or weary them
a do is a social function, here a special one

explanation.surface: Soldiers stuck on kitchen duty endure a tedious stint before some special celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just places the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatigue party is a squad of soldiers detailed to menial non-military chores such as cookhouse work.

clue.text: See cub maul ram dreadfully — a bit of an urchin

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so the preceding letters come out jumbled

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch a young animal savage a male sheep horribly, a nature-documentary moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The urchin is a sea urchin, not a street child.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulacrum is one of the radial bands of tube feet on an echinoderm such as a sea urchin.

clue.text: Credit in one week showing increase as before

indicators.note: in places the credit abbreviation inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards
CR is the standard abbreviation for credit
W abbreviates week

explanation.surface: A bank statement shows credit building up over one week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' flags an archaic spelling, and 'one' is the card rather than a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrew is an old (Spenserian) spelling of accrue, meaning to grow or accumulate.

clue.text: Err with maid getting knocked up? Did the honest thing maybe

indicators.note: knocked up in the sense of roughly put together, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man strays with a maid who falls pregnant, and he does the decent thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked up' plays on its pregnancy sense while signalling the anagram; 'doing the honest thing' is the old phrase for marrying a pregnant partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an honest woman of someone was the traditional euphemism for wedding a pregnant girlfriend.

clue.text: What's amiss with heavenly bodies circling earth? Gazes aloft

parts.note: as in 'what's up?', meaning what's wrong

indicators.note: the heavenly bodies form a ring around the abbreviation for earth

parts.note: stars are heavenly bodies
E abbreviates earth

explanation.surface: An astronomer worries about the planets orbiting Earth while staring at the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstare is an old verb meaning to look or stare upwards, so upstares is gazes skyward.

clue.text: Spinach wrapped in genipap, standard in a trat

indicators.note: something wrapped in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: lana is the wood of the genipap tree
sag (saag) is spinach in Indian cooking

explanation.surface: A recipe note: spinach wrapped in genipap, served as a regular in an Italian eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: LA(SAG)NA. A trat is a trattoria, an informal Italian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is a staple dish on the menu of almost any trattoria, so a standard there.

clue.text: Extract from Englishman entirely opposed to Scots

indicators.note: an extract is a piece taken out of a longer run of text

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An Englishman is described as wholly hostile to the Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' labels the definition as Scottish usage rather than being part of the sentence's meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots anent can mean over against or opposite, as well as concerning.

clue.text: Taxis for lawyers excessive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a line of waiting cabs, or order (the Greek sense of taxis)
second meaning: in legal usage, too great or exorbitant

explanation.walkthrough: 'For lawyers' marks the legal sense of the second meaning; barristers also have a 'cab rank rule' obliging them to take cases offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi stand is a cab queue of that name, and lawyers use the same word for an excessive claim or amount.

clue.text: Outdated matrices you'll find computer is holding

indicators.note: the following words hold the answer within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Old mathematical arrays are stored inside a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Matrices looks mathematical, but matrix is an obsolete word for the womb.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrix once meant the womb, so outdated matrices are wombs, whose Latin plural form this is.

clue.text: Sensing muscular effort I think eases a fracture

indicators.note: a fracture breaks something apart, so these letters are broken and reset

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient feels the strain in their muscles and supposes a broken bone is mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinaesthesia is the bodily sense that perceives the position and exertion of one's muscles and limbs.

clue.text: They settle disputes when accepting cases

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
ca is a dictionary abbreviation for cases

explanation.surface: Arbitrators resolve disagreements when they take on cases.
explanation.walkthrough: A(CA)S. The surface almost defines the whole answer, but the definition is just the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: ACAS is the UK's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, a public body that mediates workplace disputes.

clue.text: It helps to weigh Chinese goods, dry, in food

definitions.text: It helps to weigh Chinese goods

indicators.note: in puts the letters for dry inside the word for food

parts.note: kai is the New Zealand word for food
TT means teetotal, someone who stays off drink

explanation.surface: A merchant weighs dried Chinese produce among the food supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: KA(TT)I.
explanation.definitionFit: A katti, or catty, is a Chinese unit of weight of about 600 grams used in trade.

clue.text: Tight after imbibing number in fling

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece is swallowed inside the other

parts.note: taut means stretched tight
N is the algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: Drunk after downing a song during a wild night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunk and 'number' a song, but they are taut and N; fling is a verb, to hurl words at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling an insult is to taunt, both meaning to throw jeering words at someone.

clue.text: Anglican community in fling — it's associated with St Anthony

indicators.note: in sets the community's abbreviation inside the word for fling

parts.note: to fling is to toss
CR is the Community of the Resurrection, an Anglican religious order

explanation.surface: A monastic community is thrown into upheaval over a saint's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: T(CR)OSS, read as T-cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The T-shaped tau cross is traditionally the emblem of St Anthony the Abbot, hence St Anthony's cross.

clue.text: Active teen exercised on one

indicators.note: something exercised is worked hard and moved about, so the letters shift

parts.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: An energetic youngster works out on a single piece of gym equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Active' looks like describing the teen, but it is the definition, in the volcanic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Etnean means relating to Mount Etna, Sicily's famously active volcano, so active by association.

clue.text: Itch making one declaim, about to scratch

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for declaim goes around the next piece

parts.note: to rant is to declaim loudly
rit is a Scots verb meaning to scratch

explanation.surface: An itch makes someone loudly complain about needing to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: I + R(RIT)ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin irritation, and an irritant is the thing that causes such irritation.

clue.text: Child I kept in to learn

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside another thing

parts.note: to get something is to learn or understand it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child is kept in at school to study.
explanation.walkthrough: G(I)ET. Geit is a dialect form of get, offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A geit (or get) is an old Scots word for a child or brat, offspring in a disparaging sense.

clue.text: African stew out of place in a jet

indicators.note: letters out of place are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A North African stew seems out of place served on an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: A tajine is a slow-cooked Maghrebi stew named after the conical earthenware pot it is cooked in.

clue.text: Subject taking walk round eastern North America

indicators.note: the walk word takes the abbreviation inside it
round completes the picture of the walk going around the region

parts.note: to amble is to walk leisurely
E for eastern plus NA for North America

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a stroll around the eastern part of North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking ... round' is one split indicator; 'Subject' is an adjective here, as in subject to rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable can mean subject or answerable, as in amenable to the law.

clue.text: Religious articles, pieces held by orants moving about a bit

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it
figures moving about a bit change places, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; orants are praying figures in early Christian art
chess or draughts pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Figures at prayer shift a little while clutching sacred objects.
explanation.walkthrough: ORNA(MEN)TS.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage ornaments are the accessories of worship such as vestments and altar furnishings.

clue.text: Like fans often in trouble on circuit

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a ring is a circuit

explanation.surface: Supporters frequently get in bother at the racing circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the circuit after the trouble in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans are devotees, and their attitude toward their idols is typically worshipful.

clue.text: Mice run all over the place just the same as before

indicators.note: scattered all over the place means the letters are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mice scurry everywhere, just as they did before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' tags an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Numeric once meant identical, the very same, a sense now obsolete.

clue.text: Going back, Descartes inspires reverence — I'm impatient for last chapter

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the second piece is drawn inside
going back means the philosopher's name is read from its end

parts.note: the philosopher's first name
dread can mean awed reverence

explanation.surface: Studying philosophy in reverse, Descartes commands deep awe.
explanation.walkthrough: EN(DREAD)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An end-reader is someone too impatient to wait and turns to the final pages of a novel first.

clue.text: Fruit tree found in Ulster

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A fruit tree discovered growing in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: N(ASH)I.
explanation.definitionFit: The nashi is the Asian or Japanese pear, a crisp round fruit.

clue.text: Sailing through they half trimmed round flapping sail

indicators.note: round means surrounding the following piece
half trimmed means half of the word is cut away

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first half

indicators.note: a flapping sail moves wildly, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Yachtsmen cruising along have trimmed their flapping sail.
explanation.walkthrough: E(ASIL)Y; 'sailing through' is the idiom for passing easily.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail through a test is to pass it easily, so the phrase works as an adverb of ease.

clue.text: Rome, to its detractors, is in grip of premier after personal appearance

parts.note: PA abbreviates personal appearance

indicators.note: in the grip of means held tightly inside

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister, the premier
taken as written

explanation.surface: Critics say Rome is under the thumb of a prime minister after his public appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome' is shorthand for the Roman Catholic Church, and the definition names the term its opponents use.
explanation.definitionFit: Papism is a hostile term for Roman Catholicism, used by its opponents.

clue.text: Scotch to impress? Father maybe refusing a second

indicators.note: refusing means rejecting, so a letter is turned away

parts.note: a father is an example of a parent
the letter a, here in second place

explanation.surface: A Scottish father may refuse a second whisky while trying to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but labels the definition as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Prent is the Scots form of print, and to print can mean to impress or stamp.

clue.text: A builder in stone

parts.note: surface reading: someone constructing in stone
setter's reading: the plain description, given as the competition word to be clued by entrants

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed clue-writing competition word, so the printed clue is only a bare definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who shapes and lays stone in building.

clue.text: Mother has active husband around as nursemaid

indicators.note: the outer letters go around the word for mother

parts.note: A abbreviates active
an informal word for mother
H abbreviates husband

explanation.surface: A mother has her busy husband around to help mind the children.
explanation.walkthrough: A(MA)H; 'has' is the surface verb joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a nurse or maidservant in the Far East and India, especially one caring for children.

clue.text: Showjumping obstacle? One in the ring maybe missing

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word loses a letter

parts.note: a boxer fights in a ring

explanation.surface: A showjumping fence perhaps lacks one of the ring's competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed paper read 'missing first', so the first letter of the boxer goes; the online copy dropped that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxer is a showjumping fence made of rails, originally a hedge with a guard rail for cattle.

clue.text: Second string (from below) in settlement pharaoh left unfinished

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its final part

parts.note: pa is a Maori word for a fortified settlement
Rameses was the name of several Egyptian pharaohs

explanation.surface: A musician mentions a second string while describing an Egyptian settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek music the paramese was the string of the lyre second from the lowest, as the clue's bracket notes.

clue.text: Teacher flipped about producer of bad spelling, bursting blood vessel?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
something flipped is turned over, so the word for teacher reads backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
a hex is a witch's curse, which produces evil spells

explanation.surface: A teacher loses his temper over poor spelling, enough to burst a blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: R(HEX)IS. 'Bad spelling' suggests orthography, but it means casting evil spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhexis is the medical term for the rupture of an organ or blood vessel.

clue.text: Spaniards maybe trimming an example of Cruciferae

indicators.note: trimming cuts something away, here the next word from within

parts.note: Spaniards are examples of Iberians
the letters removed

explanation.surface: Spaniards cutting back a cabbage-family plant.
explanation.walkthrough: IBERI(AN)S with AN removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberis, the candytuft genus, belongs to the Cruciferae, the cabbage and mustard family.

clue.text: Menial Japanese displays this skin disease?

wordplay.note: an eta is a member of Japan's outcast menial class, and the word eta is T placed in EA

explanation.surface: A low-caste Japanese worker shows signs of a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA is built as T IN EA; read that description as one word and it spells the answer, so the menial 'displays this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinea is the medical name for ringworm and related fungal infections of the skin.

clue.text: Anatomical openings — Prince has bit of pus removed from both ends

indicators.note: removal from both ends strips the first and last place

parts.note: Prince Philip, the Duke of Edinburgh
the first letter of pus

explanation.surface: A prince has an abscess drained at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: PHILIP happens to start and end with the letter that 'bit of pus' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hili, plural of hilum, are the depressions where vessels and nerves enter organs such as the kidney.

clue.text: Austerity, trying with scene endlessly deteriorating

indicators.note: something deteriorating falls apart, so the letters break up and re-form
endlessly means without its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written before its tail goes

explanation.surface: Austerity is hard going, with the whole scene going downhill without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringency means severity or strictness, especially financial tightness, the essence of austerity.
